text:
alex.t: Heads up — noticed p95 tail spikes on /generate-chat after yesterday's kernel-selector rollout. Spike shows up for small prompts (<=32 tokens). Logs attached.

jess: Saw the alert. Quick glance at flamegraph -> extra memcpy in KV path when microbatch size > 1. Could be kernel_v2 memcpy pattern.

ken: Can you paste the top stack? Also did we change the fallback order for the prefetched-kv kernel?

alex.t: Pasting a short trace dump:
```
# trace snippet
batch_id=87f3
microbatch_size=2
kernel_selected=kernel_v2_causal
kv_prefetch=enabled
memcpy_ms=1.8  # up from ~0.2
scheduling_wait_ms=6.2
```

maria_r: We did nudge the selector to prefer kernel_v2 for causal when avg_seq <= 512 to reduce kernel-switch thrash. Looks like that changed perf profile for tiny requests.

jess: Interesting — kernel_v2 has faster matmul but a different KV layout that forces an extra copy on microbatch >1. That memcopy dominates when generation is short.

alex.t: Observed downstream effect: batch formation slowed because queueing attempts keep trying to assemble multi-request microbatches; token budget per-request dropped (we're slicing p95 target too aggressively) and latency increases even though throughput nominally OK.

ken: Proposed quick fix: for route tier "prod-high" and prompt length <= 64, force kernel_v1 (no extra memcpy) and set token_budget_target=20. Also change queue policy to prefer single-request flush after 40ms instead of waiting for microbatch of 2.

jess: +1 on kernel pin. Also suggest we enable KV prefetch only when prefix_cache_hit < 0.85 — avoids doing a copy for cold prefixes where prefetch doesn't help.

alex.t: Plan for canary:
- deploy kernel pin + queue-policy tweak to 10% leaf workers in prod-high
- metrics to watch: p95 latency (/generate-chat), queue_wait_ms, memcpy_ms, kernel_switch_rate, cache_hit_ratio, token_cost_per_request
- duration: 2 hours steady traffic window

ci-bot: Canary config submitted: canary_id=canary-20240228-1, targets=10%, start=1709125200

maria_r: I'll change kernel-selector threshold and add a selector metric (selected_kernel, reason) to tracing so we can correlate.

ken: I'll roll the queue policy change and add a short-circuit that flushes single-request batches if prompt_len <= 64.

jess: I'll add a perf test in the microbench harness to reproduce memcpy numbers and push a small opt to eliminate the extra copy (or short-circuit it) and open a PR.

alex.t: If telemetry shows p95 drop back to baseline and memcpy_ms falls, we keep and roll to 50% then 100%. If not, rollback immediately and we'll revert kernel-selector only.

sre-bot: Incident policy note: if p95 > 2x baseline for >5m, auto-rollout will trigger rollback. :warning:

ken: rough timeline: changes in next 90m, canary in 3h, collect 2h, decision after 5h from now. pinging @maria_r @jess for updates here.

maria_r: ack. I'll post selector metrics once in canary.

jess: ack, starting perf reproducer now. Will paste results here.

alex.t: Thanks team. Small note: also watch cost delta — increasing token_budget_target could raise cost; we want p95 first but keep an eye on token units per-req.

jess: quick perf repro (local microbench):
```
before: memcpy_ms=1.9, p95_end_to_end=210ms
after (kernel_v1): memcpy_ms=0.15, p95_end_to_end=130ms
```

alex.t: Nice. If that holds in canary then this looks good. :thumbsup:
